sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about North Macedonia.
North Macedonia is a small, friendly,
and historic country in Southeastern Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is North Macedonia?
North Macedonia is in the Balkans in Southeastern Europe.
It is next to Serbia, Kosovo, Albania, Greece, and Bulgaria.
It is a landlocked country, which means it has no sea.
What is the capital city of North Macedonia?
The capital city is Scapier.
Scapier has bridges, statues, museums, and a big old bazaar.
It is a mix of modern and traditional.
Other cities include Orid, famous for its lake and churches.
Betola, with old buildings and cafes.
Tetovo and Kumanovo.
How many people live in North Macedonia?
About 2 million people live in the country.
Most people live in cities and valleys.
The country has many ethnic groups, including Macedonians,
Albanians, Turks, Roma, and Serbs.
What language do people speak in North Macedonia?
The official languages are Macedonian, Albanian.
Some people also speak Turkish, Serbian, and Romani.
English is taught in schools and is spoken by many young people.
What is the weather like in North Macedonia?
The country has a continental climate.
Hot summers, cold winters, with snow in the mountains.
Spring and autumn are mild and pleasant.
What does North Macedonia look like?
North Macedonia has.
Tall mountains and green valleys.
Rivers, lakes, and forests.
Lake Orid, one of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe.
Villages with stone houses and red roofs.
It is perfect for hiking, camping, and exploring nature.
What animals live in North Macedonia?
In the wild, you can see, wolves, bears, and foxes.
Eagles, owls, and many songbirds.
Sheep, goats, and cows in the countryside.
The lynx is a rare and protected animal in the mountains.
What do people eat in North Macedonia?
The food is fresh, hearty, and Mediterranean inspired.
People eat bread, cheese, and yogurt.
Meat especially grilled beans, peppers, and tomatoes.
Popular dishes, top-check-graph-che baked beans,
and a clay pot, national dish.
Ivar, red pepper spread.
Shopska salad, tomatoes, cucumber, and white cheese.
Burek, pastry with cheese or meat.
Kabapi, small grilled sausages.
What do people drink in North Macedonia?
People drink water and mineral water.
Coffee, Turkish style, strong, and in small cups.
Tea, fruit juice, and yogurt drinks.
Adults may drink wine or rakija, a local fruit brandy.
North Macedonia makes very good wine.
What is life like in North Macedonia?
Life is family-based, relaxed, and community-oriented.
People enjoy going to markets and cafes,
spending time with family, listening to music,
dancing at weddings and festivals,
taking walks in the park or mountains.
What are some holidays and traditions in North Macedonia?
Independence Day, September 8, Christmas,
January 7, Orthodox calendar,
Easter with red eggs and big family meals.
Ramadan and Eid, celebrated by Muslims.
Saints Day, family or village celebrations.
People wear traditional clothes, sing, dance,
and enjoy folk music.
Some fun facts about North Macedonia.
The flag has a yellow sun on a red background.
The country became independent in 1991.
Mother Teresa was born in Scapia.
Lake Orid is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Macedonian alphabet uses Cyrillic letters.
Now you know many things about North Macedonia.
You know where it is, what people speak,
and what they eat.
You learned about nature, culture, and daily life.
Well done!
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Macedonian.
